title: On the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of the maximal multiple $ mathbb{Z} p$-extensions

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph defining the generalized Greenberg conjecture
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper says pseudo-nullity means that “any prime ideal with height less than 2 annihilates X(\tilde{k}).” This is not the definition of a pseudo-null module. Pseudo-nullity means that the localization at every prime of height at most 1 vanishes (equivalently, the support has codimension at least 2); it does not mean every such prime ideal annihilates the module. The stated condition would be vastly stronger and is nonsensical for the height-zero prime unless the module is zero.

It states that “X(k_cyc) and X(\tilde{k})” are the Galois groups of maximal unramified abelian p-extensions over “k_cyc and k, respectively.” The second base field must be \tilde{k}, not k. This directly contradicts the abstract, introduction, and Section 2.1, all of which define X(\tilde{k}) over \tilde{k}.

The bibliography supplied as the paper’s full reference list begins at [10], but the text repeatedly relies on [1]–[9], including Fröhlich [4], Fujii [5]–[8], Fukuda [9], and the classification references [1] and [2]. These sources are absent, so the citations cannot be checked and key invoked results are not properly referenced.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, first page, discussion of weak GGC
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text attributes a result to “Shinkawa [27],” while bibliography item [27] is by “T. Shirakawa,” not Shinkawa. This is a wrong attribution.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 4.1.3 and its proof; downstream use in Lemma 4.1.4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated orbit is impossible: it says \(\sigma|_k(D_1)=D_2\), \((\sigma|_k)^2(D_1)=D_3\), but \((\sigma|_k)^3(D_1)=D_1\). Since \(\sigma^3\) is explicitly identified as complex conjugation, it must send \(D_1\) to \(\overline D_1\), not \(D_1\). Moreover, (4.1) defines \(\mathfrak P_2=\sigma(\mathfrak P_1)\), whereas the proof asserts \(\sigma(D_{\mathfrak P_1})=D_{\overline{\mathfrak P}_2}\). Lemma 4.1.4 then uses a different orbit again, beginning \(\sigma(D_1)=\overline D_2\). Thus the prime/decomposition-group action used to derive the degree-six parameterization is internally inconsistent, invalidating the displayed decomposition-group formulas and later calculations based on them.

predicted_errors.error_location: Corollary 4.1.6, proof, displayed rank equivalences for \(\overline{A'}\)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The presentation matrix \(A'\) is 4-by-4 and has first row \((1,0,0,0)\). Consequently, \(A(k)=0\) requires \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_p}\overline{A'}=4\), a cyclic cokernel requires rank 3, and a two-dimensional \(A(k)/pA(k)\) requires rank 2. The paper instead writes ranks 3, 2, and 1. Those ranks would apply to the lower-right 3-by-3 block \(A\), not to \(A'\) as claimed. The proof as written is therefore false.

The lemma defines \(K\leftrightarrow\langle I_1,I_1,I_2,I_2\rangle\), duplicating the unbarred inertia groups. It then claims that \(K/k\) is unramified outside \(\{p_3,\overline p_3\}\), which would require killing the inertia at both \(p_1,\overline p_1,p_2,\overline p_2\), i.e. barred groups as well. As written, the subgroup does not include \(\overline I_1\) or \(\overline I_2\), so the asserted ramification statement and the finite-index conclusion do not follow.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 4.1.8, final paragraph of the proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The lemma statement correctly says \(\mathcal K(G)=0\) iff \(|K|\not\equiv0\pmod p\). But the final sentence of the proof says \(K(G)=0\) iff the displayed determinant \(|K|\equiv0\pmod p\). For a cokernel presented by the square matrix, triviality requires full rank modulo p, hence a determinant that is a p-adic unit, not one congruent to zero. This is both an internal contradiction and the wrong criterion.

For totally imaginary \((2,2)\)-extensions of \(\mathbb Q\), the paper says that it can prove the main theorem and that it will “only write each object down in Table 1.” No Table 1 appears anywhere in the supplied full paper, and no proof of this quartic case follows before Section 4 starts. Since Theorem 1.1.1 claims a complete classification for all degree-4 CM fields, including this case, that portion of the claimed proof is absent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4, paragraph after the unnamed Lemma 4.4.4 proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paragraph begins, “Next, we show that \(p\) is unramified in \(k_\infty/k\),” but its conclusion is “\(P_\infty Q_\infty/k_\infty\) is an unramified extension, which implies that \(p\) is ramified in \(k_\infty/k\).” These are opposite assertions. The subsequent application requires ramification, so the stated goal is inconsistent with the argument and must be corrected.

The final sentence is incomplete: “If there should exist a CM-field \(k\) with \([k:\mathbb Q]\ge4\) which satisfies the following, then …” but no following conditions are supplied. It therefore presents an unsupported conditional conclusion with its hypothesis missing, leaving the claimed implication uninterpretable.
